overview: White plays a Stonewall or reversed-Dutch style set-up, putting pawns on d4 and f4 and aiming for e3, Nf3 and Bd3 with a kingside focus. Black can take the centre with ...d5 and ...e6 or ...c5 and play on the weakened e1-h4 diagonal and e4. I am unsure of the theory and judge it from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: Stonewall-style set-up with e3, Nf3, Bd3 and a kingside attack
Control e5 with f4 and keep a solid pawn wall

black_ideas.idea: Claim the centre with ...d5, ...e6 and ...c5, and attack d4
Use the weakened e1-h4 diagonal and e4 square, ...Ne4 ideas

typical_structures.structure: White Stonewall pawns c3/d4/e3/f4 against Black's ...d5/...e6 centre

character.notes: A slightly eccentric but steady pawn wall; neither side forced into tactics early.

soundness.notes: Playable but loosens the kingside; not refuted.

structure.notes: Stonewall-like pawn wall, but centre not locked early.

approach.notes: Strong players hardly ever choose 2.f4 against the Indian.

level.notes: Few concrete lines but plans are not trivial.

character.reason: Quirky but steady play with neither side forced into sharp lines.

level.reason: Few lines but the kingside weakness takes care.

plans.reason: White sets up f4 with d4 and e3.
